prompt: What is Robin Williams's rule for contrast?

choices.text: Use as many colours as the data has categories
choices.why: That makes everything equally loud.

choices.text: If two elements differ, make them very different
choices.why: Weak differences create doubt instead of order.

choices.text: Make the title a little bigger than the text below it
choices.why: A little bigger is the timid contrast the lesson warns against.

choices.text: Black on white only
choices.why: Not the rule, and too narrow.

prompt: What does contrast decide on a slide, in the hierarchy sense?
hint: The eye goes to the loudest thing first.

choices.text: Which colours the company brand allows on a slide used in a meeting
choices.why: Brand rules are a separate matter.

choices.text: How many slides the deck needs
choices.why: Contrast works inside a slide.

choices.text: The size of the projector screen in the room
choices.why: That is the room, not the design.

choices.text: The reading order
choices.why: Claim, evidence, source, in that order, instead of left to chance.

prompt: WCAG's minimum contrast ratio for ordinary text is how many to 1?
Why design for the worst room you will present in?

choices.text: Projectors fade colours; rooms are bright
choices.why: So use darker text, larger type and fewer subtle shades.

choices.text: To impress the most senior person in the meeting room
choices.why: Not the reason.

choices.text: Because the room decides which template must be used
choices.why: They do not.

choices.text: It saves printing
choices.why: Printing is not involved.

prompt: What is Williams's principle of alignment?

choices.text: Centre everything on the slide
choices.why: Centring is the weakest alignment for text.

choices.text: Every element connects visually to something else
choices.why: Usually an edge or a centre line shared with another element.

choices.text: Put the chart on the right
choices.why: Position is free; connection is not.

choices.text: Align numbers by the decimal point
choices.why: Good practice in a table, and not the principle.

prompt: Why is centred text weak for anything longer than a title?

choices.text: It wastes space on the left and the right, which shrinks the font
choices.why: Space is not the issue.

choices.text: It is harder to print
choices.why: No.

choices.text: Projectors cut the middle
choices.why: They crop edges, not the middle.

choices.text: Both edges are ragged
choices.why: The eye has to find the start of every line afresh.

prompt: What happens when the grid moves between slides?

choices.text: The slide jumps on every advance
choices.why: A small cost paid on every slide.

choices.text: Nothing
choices.why: The jump is visible.

choices.text: The slides take longer to load on an older laptop
choices.why: Not a technical issue.

choices.text: The colours change
choices.why: That is repetition, a different principle.

prompt: Which repetition matters most for data, by the lesson?
hint: Slide 4 teaches it, slide 5 relies on it.

choices.text: The same font on every slide
choices.why: It helps, and is not the most important.

choices.text: The logo on every slide, in the same corner, so the brand is consistent
choices.why: Decoration, and the template handles it.

choices.text: Colour keeping its meaning
choices.why: Late first delivery in one colour on every slide where it appears.

choices.text: Same number of bullets
choices.why: Not a principle anywhere.

prompt: On the third slide of Marina's first deck, the colour that meant late now means the capital. What does the reader do?

choices.text: Reads the legend carefully
choices.why: Readers rarely re-check a meaning they think they know.

choices.text: Misreads it, carrying the old meaning
choices.why: That is why a colour should mean one thing in the whole deck.

choices.text: Asks the presenter to stop
choices.why: They do not notice the switch.

choices.text: Ignores colour entirely and reads only the numbers printed on each bar
choices.why: Nobody reads that way by default.

prompt: A company template is in place. What does it not do for you?
hint: It does not know your data.

choices.text: Set the fonts
choices.why: It does.

choices.text: Place the title
choices.why: It does.

choices.text: Put the logo on every page of the deck in the corner chosen by the brand team
choices.why: It does that too.

choices.text: Know what your colours mean
choices.why: Write a small legend for the whole deck before the first chart.

prompt: How are the three number-label pairs grouped on the right of the figure?

choices.why: Space alone says which label belongs to which number.

choices.text: By a box drawn around each pair
choices.why: No boxes were drawn.

choices.text: By giving each pair its own colour

choices.text: By thin lines between the pairs

prompt: How much margin does the lesson suggest keeping?

choices.text: None: use the whole slide
choices.why: Edges get cropped and text there looks as if it is falling off.

choices.text: About a twentieth of the width
choices.why: Nothing closer than that to the edge.

choices.text: Exactly two centimetres in every slide tool, whatever the size of the slide
choices.why: The lesson gives a proportion, not a fixed length.

choices.text: Half the slide
choices.why: That is not a margin.

prompt: Guy Kawasaki's rule of thumb sets the smallest font at how many points?
Why did Amazon replace slides with narrative memos, by the lesson?

choices.text: Memos are cheaper to make
choices.why: Not the reasoning.

choices.text: Executives could not see the projector
choices.why: No.

choices.text: Slides were banned by law
choices.why: No law involved.

choices.text: Full sentences force the writer to connect the ideas
choices.why: Bullets let ideas sit side by side unconnected.

prompt: Your deck will be sent ahead and read by people who will not attend. Which advice from this lesson changes?

choices.text: Keep one colour for late deliveries
choices.why: Repetition holds either way.

choices.text: Align to a grid
choices.why: Alignment holds either way.

choices.text: How much text it carries
choices.why: A read deck needs full sentences, definitions and caveats; nobody is there to explain.

choices.text: Keep margins of about a twentieth of the slide's width on every side
choices.why: Margins help a reader too.
